$comment: Songs are MIDI-note based so black keys work. Each phrase holds the sustain pedal for its duration. `seq` entries are arrays of simultaneous MIDI notes.

songs.title: Bach — Prelude in C, BWV 846 (mm. 1–4)
songs.why: Proven default. All white keys, steady sixteenth-note figuration, sounds musical even on a rough engine, and the arpeggiation exercises repeat/overlap and the sustain pedal.

songs.title: Beethoven — Ode to Joy
songs.why: Instantly recognizable, all white keys, mostly stepwise. Good when you want the melody legible rather than showing off polyphony.

songs.title: Beethoven — Für Elise (opening)
songs.why: Uses black keys (D#5), so it proves the keybed maps accidentals correctly. Pick this when black-key fidelity is the point.

songs.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
songs.why: Simplest possible sanity check — all white keys, wide leaps, no fast passages. Use when an artifact is fragile and you just need it to sound like something.
